issues.legal_issue: A landlord’s acceptance of rent after serving a notice to quit does not, by itself, waive the notice when the landlord continues to pursue eviction and there is no other evidence of an intention to treat the lease as subsisting.
material_facts: The landlord served two notices terminating the tenancy and later brought an eviction suit.
The tenant tendered, and the landlord accepted, rent for months after the notices, including while the eviction suit was pending.
The landlord continued to prosecute the eviction suit, and no other fact or circumstance supported the claim that the landlord intended to treat the lease as subsisting.
The tenant’s review petition was dismissed, and the appeal challenged that dismissal.
issues.conclusion: The rent acceptance alone did not waive the notices to quit; the landlord’s continued pursuit of eviction and the absence of other evidence showed no intention to treat the lease as subsisting. The appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 111(h) and 113 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, waiver requires the express or implied consent of the recipient of the notice and an act by the person who gave it that shows an intention to treat the lease as subsisting. Whether such an intention is shown is a question of fact determined from all relevant circumstances; acceptance of rent is not determinative by itself. The Court rejected the overly broad proposition in AIR 1926 Calcutta 763 that accepting rent after notice necessarily waives the notice. It also referred by analogy to an earlier Supreme Court decision concerning Section 116, which held that acceptance of rent alone did not signify assent to continuation of a lease after its expiry.

rule.if: eviction_case_after_notice and rent_accepted_after_notice and eviction_proceeding_pursued and no_other_evidence_of_intention

predicates.eviction_case_after_notice: A landlord brought an eviction proceeding after giving a notice to quit.
predicates.rent_accepted_after_notice: The landlord accepted rent tendered by the tenant after giving the notice to quit.
predicates.eviction_proceeding_pursued: The landlord continued to pursue the eviction proceeding after accepting the rent.
predicates.no_other_evidence_of_intention: There was no other evidence that the landlord intended to treat the lease as subsisting.

issues.definition: When a landlord pursues an eviction proceeding after notice, accepts rent tendered afterward, and there is no other evidence of an intention to continue the lease, the notice is not waived.
